The pacing is uneven, with long stretches of dialogue and exposition that do little to advance the plot or develop the characters.

The emotional depth that was present in the earlier books is also sorely lacking in 'Mockingjay'. The relationships between Katniss and her fellow characters feel shallow and contrived, with little emotional resonance. The romantic subplot between Katniss and Peeta, which was once a compelling and complex aspect of the series, is reduced to a series of trite conversations and declarations of love.

In short, 'Mockingjay' is a disappointing conclusion to a series that once showed so much promise. If you're looking for a truly satisfying conclusion to a dystopian trilogy, I would recommend looking elsewhere.

The thematic elements of 'The Fault in Our Stars' are also problematic.
